summary: A fifth teaching period, 'Layering: new fields under a settled canon, c. 2000–', joins the period list, and six entries whose consolidation falls after 1985 or 2000 receive a period: settler colonialism, the liberal order framework, Canada's 1960s, digital history and web history to the new period; the languages of class debate to 'Further turns, c. 1985–2000'. No entry, edge or source text changes. The period's name states what the History PhD citation graph (release 2026-10-23) shows for the years after 2000: the theory canon of 1963–98 persists as a shared floor (Foucault cited by 17% of theses, Anderson 11%, Thompson and Joan Scott 6% each, in every cohort since 2010), no later debate is co-cited by more than 3% of theses, and a layer of regional frameworks and fields (the archive, settler colonial studies, environmental history, empire and sovereignty, the history of capitalism) was added under the floor rather than replacing it.
authorization: User, 2026-10-23: 'use this information to build out the atlas (that we don't call an atlas anymore)', after the cohort analysis in data/field-research/dissertation-citations-2026-10-11/summary/cohorts/README.md (§§1–6) and the user's reading that the historiographical narrative is still the 1980s debate, that 'there is no new big debate that everyone feels the need to cite', and that new fields (environmental history, settler colonial studies, the history of emotions) are the change.
rationale: The frame has been open since revision 1.133 (scope.frame; each entry carries coverage.reviewed_through), but the teaching-period list still ended at 'Further turns, c. 1985–2000', so entries consolidated after 2000 sat under 'No assigned period'. The citation analysis gives the period its character: layering, not a new debate. Period assignments follow each entry's own chronology: settler_colonialism (Wolfe 1999, 2006; Veracini 2010; the journal 2011; critiques 2012–20), liberal_order_framework (McKay's prospectus 2000; the 2009 debate), cdn_sixties (Owram 1996 as the early account; Palmer 2009, Mills 2010, the 2013 collection), digital_history (publications 2003–22), web_history (2003–26) are c. 2000– fields; languages_of_class (Languages of Class 1983, the ILWCH forum 1987, Visions of the People 1991, the end-of-social-history round 1995–96) belongs with the further turns of c. 1985–2000. capitalismdebates (1944–2023) and the enduring fields stay unassigned by design. The applier gains periods_set (guarded like layers_set; the prior list is kept in the acceptance record) and period joins the field_sets allow-list.
